signature.instructions: Decide whether two business listings refer to the SAME physical place. You are given place A (input_name, input_address) and place B (match_name, match_address), plus the geographic distance between their coordinates (typically in meters; small numbers mean 'close'). Return is_same=True only if both listings plausibly denote the same real-world business location. Key rules: (1) Different street numbers on the same street almost always mean DIFFERENT places, even if names are similar. (2) Very different names (different brand words, different chains, different cuisines) at the same address usually mean DIFFERENT places — a single address can host multiple businesses (e.g. a stadium contains many concession stands / sections; a mall contains many stores; an office tower contains many tenants). Numbered sub-locations like 'SECTION 149', 'GATE 5', 'SUITE 200', 'STAND #12' inside a venue are DIFFERENT places from each other and from the venue itself. (3) Minor name variations (spelling, punctuation, suffixes like 'restaurant', 'inc', 'llc', 'the', apostrophes, singular/plural, store numbers like '#72', abbreviations 'st'/'street', 'ave'/'avenue') with the SAME street number and street usually mean the SAME place. (4) Large distance (well beyond geocoding jitter, e.g. > ~100 meters) with clearly differing addresses => DIFFERENT. (5) When genuinely ambiguous, weigh name similarity, address similarity, and distance together. Reply with a boolean.

module_src:
class SamePlaceModule(dspy.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.predict = dspy.Predict(dspy.Signature(
            'input_name: str, input_address: str, match_name: str, match_address: str, distance: float -> is_same: bool',
            "Decide whether two business listings refer to the SAME physical place. "
            "You are given place A (input_name, input_address) and place B (match_name, match_address), "
            "plus the geographic distance between their coordinates (typically in meters; small numbers mean 'close'). "
            "Return is_same=True only if both listings plausibly denote the same real-world business location. "
            "Key rules: "
            "(1) Different street numbers on the same street almost always mean DIFFERENT places, even if names are similar. "
            "(2) Very different names (different brand words, different chains, different cuisines) at the same address "
            "usually mean DIFFERENT places — a single address can host multiple businesses (e.g. a stadium contains many "
            "concession stands / sections; a mall contains many stores; an office tower contains many tenants). "
            "Numbered sub-locations like 'SECTION 149', 'GATE 5', 'SUITE 200', 'STAND #12' inside a venue are DIFFERENT places "
            "from each other and from the venue itself. "
            "(3) Minor name variations (spelling, punctuation, suffixes like 'restaurant', 'inc', 'llc', 'the', apostrophes, "
            "singular/plural, store numbers like '#72', abbreviations 'st'/'street', 'ave'/'avenue') with the SAME street "
            "number and street usually mean the SAME place. "
            "(4) Large distance (well beyond geocoding jitter, e.g. > ~100 meters) with clearly differing addresses => DIFFERENT. "
            "(5) When genuinely ambiguous, weigh name similarity, address similarity, and distance together. "
            "Reply with a boolean."
        ))

    def forward(self, **inputs):
        import re
        import difflib

        input_name = str(inputs.get("input_name", "") or "")
        input_address = str(inputs.get("input_address", "") or "")
        match_name = str(inputs.get("match_name", "") or "")
        match_address = str(inputs.get("match_address", "") or "")
        try:
            distance = float(inputs.get("distance", 0.0) or 0.0)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            distance = 0.0

        STREET_SYNONYMS = {
            "st": "street", "str": "street", "street": "street",
            "ave": "avenue", "av": "avenue", "avenue": "avenue",
            "blvd": "boulevard", "boulevard": "boulevard",
            "rd": "road", "road": "road",
            "dr": "drive", "drive": "drive",
            "ln": "lane", "lane": "lane",
            "ct": "court", "court": "court",
            "pl": "place", "place": "place",
            "pkwy": "parkway", "parkway": "parkway",
            "hwy": "highway", "highway": "highway",
            "cir": "circle", "circle": "circle",
            "ter": "terrace", "terrace": "terrace",
            "sq": "square", "square": "square",
            "way": "way",
            "n": "north", "s": "south", "e": "east", "w": "west",
            "north": "north", "south": "south", "east": "east", "west": "west",
            "ne": "northeast", "nw": "northwest", "se": "southeast", "sw": "southwest",
            "ste": "suite", "suite": "suite", "apt": "apartment", "apartment": "apartment",
            "unit": "unit", "#": "number",
        }

        NAME_STOPWORDS = {
            "the", "a", "an", "and", "of", "&",
            "restaurant", "restaurants", "cafe", "caf", "bar", "grill",
            "inc", "llc", "ltd", "co", "company", "corp", "corporation",
            "shop", "store", "market",
        }

        # Words that signal a numbered sub-location inside a larger venue.
        # If one name has such a marker with a number and the other doesn't (or has a different number),
        # they are DIFFERENT places even at the same address.
        SUBLOCATION_MARKERS = {
            "section", "sec", "gate", "stand", "booth", "kiosk",
            "suite", "ste", "unit", "apt", "apartment", "room", "rm",
            "floor", "fl", "level", "lvl", "bldg", "building",
            "bleachers", "bleacher", "concourse", "concession",
        }

        def normalize_text(s):
            s = s.lower()
            s = re.sub(r"[^\w\s#]", " ", s)
            s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
            return s

        def normalize_address_tokens(addr):
            s = normalize_text(addr)
            toks = []
            for t in s.split():
                toks.append(STREET_SYNONYMS.get(t, t))
            return toks

        def extract_street_number(addr_tokens):
            for t in addr_tokens:
                if t.isdigit():
                    return t
            return None

        def strip_store_number_from_name(name):
            # Remove tokens like "#72", "#130" — these are store-number suffixes,
            # not sub-location markers, and shouldn't count as name differences.
            s = re.sub(r"#\s*\d+", " ", name)
            return s

        def normalize_name_tokens(name):
            s = normalize_text(strip_store_number_from_name(name))
            toks = []
            for t in s.split():
                if t in NAME_STOPWORDS:
                    continue
                toks.append(t)
            return toks

        def extract_sublocation_numbers(name):
            """Find numbers that follow a sub-location marker word, e.g. 'section 149' -> {'149'}."""
            s = normalize_text(strip_store_number_from_name(name))
            toks = s.split()
            nums = set()
            for i, t in enumerate(toks):
                if t in SUBLOCATION_MARKERS:
                    # find next numeric token within a small window
                    for j in range(i + 1, min(i + 3, len(toks))):
                        if toks[j].isdigit():
                            nums.add(toks[j])
                            break
            return nums

        def has_sublocation_marker(name):
            s = normalize_text(strip_store_number_from_name(name))
            return any(t in SUBLOCATION_MARKERS for t in s.split())

        def jaccard(a, b):
            sa, sb = set(a), set(b)
            if not sa and not sb:
                return 1.0
            if not sa or not sb:
                return 0.0
            return len(sa & sb) / len(sa | sb)

        def char_ratio(a, b):
            return difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio()

        a_addr_toks = normalize_address_tokens(input_address)
        b_addr_toks = normalize_address_tokens(match_address)
        a_num = extract_street_number(a_addr_toks)
        b_num = extract_street_number(b_addr_toks)

        a_addr_norm = " ".join(a_addr_toks)
        b_addr_norm = " ".join(b_addr_toks)

        a_name_stripped = strip_store_number_from_name(input_name)
        b_name_stripped = strip_store_number_from_name(match_name)
        a_name_norm = " ".join(normalize_text(a_name_stripped).split())
        b_name_norm = " ".join(normalize_text(b_name_stripped).split())

        a_name_toks = normalize_name_tokens(input_name)
        b_name_toks = normalize_name_tokens(match_name)

        name_jac = jaccard(a_name_toks, b_name_toks)
        name_char = char_ratio(a_name_norm, b_name_norm)
        addr_jac = jaccard(a_addr_toks, b_addr_toks)
        addr_char = char_ratio(a_addr_norm, b_addr_norm)

        a_sub_nums = extract_sublocation_numbers(input_name)
        b_sub_nums = extract_sublocation_numbers(match_name)
        a_has_sub = has_sublocation_marker(input_name)
        b_has_sub = has_sublocation_marker(match_name)

        # ---- Deterministic decisions ----

        # Rule A: different street numbers (both present and differ) -> different.
        if a_num is not None and b_num is not None and a_num != b_num:
            return dspy.Prediction(is_same=False)

        # Rule B: sub-location markers indicate different sub-parts of the same venue.
        # If both have sub-location markers with differing numbers -> different.
        if a_sub_nums and b_sub_nums and a_sub_nums != b_sub_nums:
            return dspy.Prediction(is_same=False)
        # If exactly one side has a sub-location marker (e.g. "SECTION 149") and the
        # other doesn't, and the names are otherwise quite different, they refer to a
        # sub-part vs. either the venue or a different sub-part -> different.
        if (a_has_sub != b_has_sub) and name_jac < 0.5 and name_char < 0.6:
            return dspy.Prediction(is_same=False)

        # Rule C: same street number AND very similar addresses AND very similar names -> same.
        same_number = (a_num is not None and a_num == b_num)
        addr_very_similar = (addr_char >= 0.85 or addr_jac >= 0.8)
        name_very_similar = (name_char >= 0.85 or name_jac >= 0.7)

        if same_number and addr_very_similar and name_very_similar:
            return dspy.Prediction(is_same=True)

        # Rule D: identical normalized names AND identical normalized addresses -> same.
        if a_name_norm == b_name_norm and a_addr_norm == b_addr_norm:
            return dspy.Prediction(is_same=True)

        # Rule E: names extremely different at same address (or nearby) -> different.
        # Different businesses can share an address.
        if name_char < 0.4 and name_jac < 0.25:
            return dspy.Prediction(is_same=False)

        # Rule F: addresses very different and no shared street number -> different.
        if not same_number and addr_char < 0.4 and addr_jac < 0.2:
            return dspy.Prediction(is_same=False)

        # Rule G: large distance with non-matching addresses -> different.
        if distance > 150.0 and not (same_number and addr_very_similar):
            return dspy.Prediction(is_same=False)

        # Ambiguous -> fall back to LLM.
        result = self.predict(
            input_name=input_name,
            input_address=input_address,
            match_name=match_name,
            match_address=match_address,
            distance=distance,
        )
        try:
            is_same = bool(result.is_same)
        except Exception:
            val = str(getattr(result, "is_same", "")).strip().lower()
            is_same = val in ("true", "1", "yes", "y", "t")
        return dspy.Prediction(is_same=is_same)
